Causes: (1) FY2020 equity of 56,060 was inflated by the all-stock TD Ameritrade acquisition, (2) AOCI swung from positive to -14.8B in 2022-24 as rates rose, (3) $4.5B of preferred redeemed 2025-26 and >100% payout via buybacks. scenario_narratives.base: Schwab's value turns on three things: (1) organic asset gathering - core NNA running ~5.5-6% a year on $13.3T of client assets (Q3-2026 $190.4B, +38% YoY; October a record $66.5B), the #1 RIA custody franchise and 40M active brokerage accounts; (2) net interest revenue (~half of revenue), where NIM reached 3.04% in Q3 and the adjusted pretax margin 54.8% - the base case now starts FY2027 at 53.5%, just under the FY2026E level of ~53.8%, and still gives the margin back to 51% by FY2031 as Fed easing narrows new-money spreads and lending growth is funded with costlier wholesale money; (3) capital return - which slowed in Q3 (buybacks $500M, ~70% payout year to date) because loan and margin growth is consuming capital at a 7.0% adjusted leverage ratio, so FY2027-28 retention is raised to 1.0x/0.9x revenue growth before reverting to 0.8x. Revenue grows 8% in FY2027 fading to 3.5% by FY2036. Valued as FCFE at a 10% cost of equity with the $6.2B preferred deducted, the base case sits modestly above the current price.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Q3-2026 run-rate proves to be a floor: record NNA sustains 6-7% organic growth, BDA balances keep migrating onto Schwab's balance sheet and legacy low-yield securities reprice into record lending, so the adjusted pretax margin holds 54.8% in FY2027 and settles at 55% - the operating leverage a fully integrated TDA platform should deliver. AOCI pull-to-par resumes and releases capital, so retention falls to 0.6x growth and payout runs near 100%. Revenue grows 11% in FY2027, 4% by FY2036, terminal growth 3.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: 2023 repeats in milder form: short rates stay elevated relative to sweep yields, clients sort cash into money-market funds, and Schwab re-levers onto FHLB and brokered funding while a market drawdown cuts fee and trading revenue. FY2027 revenue falls 6%, the adjusted pretax margin drops to 43% (FY2024 was ~41.5%), buybacks pause to rebuild leverage capital, and the franchise then grows only 3-4.5% with the margin recovering to 46%. Exit at 12x FCFE. No solvency element - the RIA and retail franchise is intact; this is an earnings reset and a de-rating, not a credit event.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Schwab is a savings-and-loan holding company whose economics are those of a deposit-funded bank wrapped around a fee-earning brokerage and custody franchise, so it is valued as free cash flow to equity - adjusted net income (before non-cash amortization of TD Ameritrade intangibles) less the capital retained to grow the balance sheet at its leverage target - capitalised at a 10% USD cost of equity. Deposits, FHLB advances and senior notes are operating funding already charged inside net interest revenue, so net debt is zero and only the $6.2B preferred is deducted ahead of common. FY0 is the FY2026 estimate (nine months reported); the three cases differ on whether the post-2023 net-interest-margin recovery holds, extends or reverses through another cash-sorting episode.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cash sorting: if short-term rates stay elevated versus sweep yields, client cash migrates to money-market funds and Schwab re-levers onto costlier FHLB/brokered funding, compressing net interest revenue (~half of revenue) - the bear case's FY2027 -6% revenue and 43% margin
Rate path: Fed easing narrows the spread on new asset purchases even as funding costs fall; the base case already gives back 150bps of margin from FY2029
Equity-market levels drive asset-management fees and trading activity (~40% of revenue combined); a 20% drawdown would cut both with little cost offset

AOCI (-$11.2B at Sep-26, wider than June's -$10.6B) depresses tangible common equity to ~$15/share; if regulation (Basel III endgame for Category III firms) forces AOCI into regulatory capital before pull-to-par completes, buybacks slow and retention rises

The model excludes ~$560M/yr of acquired-intangible amortization (and, in FY2026, ~$50M of Forge integration cost) from the flows; that is correct for FCFE but means the valuation sits on adjusted, not GAAP, earnings (GAAP EPS ~$0.25/yr lower)

The share count is held flat and buybacks are treated as the distribution channel; per-share value is therefore insensitive to repurchase pace but sensitive to the 10% cost of equity and the 0.8x retention ratio (see sensitivity grid)

Capital intensity of growth: Q3-2026 buybacks fell to $500M with adjusted Tier 1 leverage at the top of its 6.75-7.00% objective; if loan and margin growth keep outrunning deposits beyond FY2028, the base case's reversion to 0.8x retention is too generous (each 0.1 of k held for all ten years is worth roughly $1/share)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY0 = FY2026E total net revenues. Nine months reported: 20,725 (Q1 6,482, Q2 7,072, Q3 7,171; +18% YoY) plus a Q4 estimate of ~7,275 (+1.5% on Q3, +14.8% on Q4-2025's 6,336: record October core NNA and margin balances against a $7.0B seasonal fall in transactional sweep cash and lower floating-rate yields). 28,000 is +17.1% on FY2025's 23,921. The prior build carried 28,200 on H1 actuals with Q3 pencilled at 7,250; Q3 printed 79 lower and management said revenue/NIM are tracking toward the lower end of its raised ranges, so Q4 is trimmed too. CAUTION: the Analysis JSON quotes FY2026 revenue-growth guidance of 14-15%; that cannot be the current range - it would require Q4 revenue of 6,550-6,780, a 5-9% sequential fall - so it is treated as a superseded or misquoted figure and NOT used. Schwab's 10-Q gives no revenue guidance; FY0 remains a run-rate estimate.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 10-Q cover-page common shares outstanding 1,726,007,705 as of 2026-10-30 (Q3-2026 10-Q, after 9M-2026 buybacks of 40.2M shares for $3,877M) plus ~5.0M dilutive awards (Q3-2026 diluted 1,733M less basic 1,728M weighted average). One common class (TD Bank's nonvoting stake was sold and converted in 2025). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed inside compensation, and buybacks are the FCFE distribution channel, not a separately modelled count reduction.
inputs.net_debt_note: Bank convention (house precedent NAB.AX, HBAN, NTRS, GL): bank deposits ($244.1B at 2026-09-30), FHLB borrowings ($2.0B), other short-term borrowings ($14.2B) and long-term debt ($23.8B, senior notes plus a $633M software-licence liability) are operating funding of a savings-and-loan holding company, serviced inside net interest revenue. FCFE is post-interest, so net debt is held at 0 and the flows are capitalised at the cost of equity. Cash ($36.7B; $68.5B including restricted/segregated) is likewise operating liquidity of the bank and broker-dealer, not surplus. The only claim senior to common deducted is the $6,213M of preferred stock (equity_bridge).
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is the FY2026E FCFE proxy: adjusted net income 11,524 (adjusted pretax 15,064 = 53.8% of 28,000 - 9M actual 11,098 = GAAP pretax 10,634 + acquired-intangible amortization 415 + Forge acquisition/integration costs 49, plus Q4 at ~54.5% - taxed at 23.5%) less ~2,300 of capital retention. Retention is now read off the 9M-2026 actuals rather than the prior build's formula (0.8 x a normalised 6% growth = 1,354): net income to common 7,889 less 5,554 returned and 575 of net preferred retired leaves ~1,760 retained in nine months. reported_fcf is the CSV's FY2025 OCF-less-capex (8,709); it is deposit/brokerage-flow noise for this business (9M-2026 OCF 13,256 on client-payable swings) and is recorded for auditability only. The owner-FCF identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income deliberately does NOT hold on this route.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL ShareBasedCompensation: FY2025 $317M (1.33% of revenue); 9M-2026 $295M per the Q3-2026 10-Q cash flow statement (1.42% of 20,725; 9M-2025 259). No separate net-share-settlement withholding figure is tagged; it is treated as part of buyback cash. SBC sits inside compensation expense, so the pretax margin is post-SBC; sbc_pct_path is carried so the engine's house/street band is computed.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: net interest revenue IS the business (~$11.75B FY2025, 49% of net revenues). Nothing is added back as net cash, so there is no double count.
inputs.buyback_note: TTM to 2026-09-30: FY2025 7,346 - 9M-2025 4,581 + 9M-2026 3,877 = $6,642M. The pace SLOWED sharply: Q1-2026 $2,378M, Q2 $999M, Q3 $500M (4.7M shares); $10.6B remains on the $20B authorisation. 9M-2026 return to common = buybacks 3,877 + common dividends ~1,677 = ~5,554, i.e. ~70% of the 7,889 net income to common (FY2025: 111%; H1-2026: 89%), plus a net $575M of preferred retired (Series I redeemed 2,055, Series L issued 1,480). The slowdown is balance-sheet growth absorbing capital - bank loans +25% YTD to $72.3B, margin receivables +22% to $128.1B, total assets +6% YTD - with the adjusted Tier 1 leverage ratio at 7.0%, the top of the 6.75-7.00% operating objective, so there is no excess to release. Quarterly dividend $0.32 ($1.28 annualised).
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is the FY2026 estimate (fiscal year closes 31 Dec 2026; nine months reported, Q4 due mid-January 2027), so Y1 = FY2027. Last fully reported year is FY2025.

balance_sheet_anchors.note: All from the Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet (2026-09-30). TCE computed as before (equity - preferred - goodwill - acquired intangibles, no deferred-tax add-back). AOCI did NOT continue to pull to par: -11,206 at Sep-26 vs -10,983 at Dec-25 and -10,575 at Jun-26, so the capital release the bull case leans on slipped a quarter. Wholesale funding has edged back up as lending outpaced deposits (FHLB 2.0B vs 0.5B at June; other short-term borrowings 14.2B vs 6.9B at Dec-25; deposits down 11.6B YTD).

inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 10.0% in USD: 10-yr UST ~4.25%, equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~1.15. Above NTRS's 9.75% because SCHW's net interest revenue (~half of revenue) carries the cash-sorting/deposit-duration risk that produced the 2023 episode, and the AOCI hole still sits against tangible book. One rate across all three scenarios, so risk is charged once, through the scenario paths and weights. Labelled 'wacc' only because that is the engine field; no debt is in the capital structure being discounted.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (branches, offices) are expensed inside occupancy/equipment expense and therefore inside the pretax margin; no lease liability is added to net debt (treatment A, applied once).
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; net income is fully attributable to the parent.
inputs.engine_mapping: The component engine is driven as a bank P&L: 'EBITDA margin' = ADJUSTED pretax margin + D&A % + SBC %, so that EBITDA - SBC - D&A = adjusted pretax income (GAAP pretax + amortization of acquired intangibles: FY2025 11,459 + 512 = 11,971 = 50.0% of revenue; 9M-2026 10,634 + 415 + 49 Forge integration = 11,098 = 53.5%; Q3-2026 3,928 = 54.8%). Acquired-intangible amortization (~$560M/yr incl. Forge, mostly TD Ameritrade customer relationships, $7.1B left) is non-cash and requires no reinvestment, so excluding it is what an FCFE basis requires; it is not capitalised beyond its run-off because terminal flows are built on the same adjusted margin only as a matter of definition - see key risks. cash_tax_rate 23.5% (GAAP effective FY2025 22.8%, 9M-2026 23.0%, Q3 23.1%) applies to adjusted pretax. D&A and core capex share a 2.3% core (FY2025 capex 548 = 2.3% of revenue; depreciation runs above capex post-integration, so D&A=capex is conservative), and the EXCESS of capex_pct over da_pct is the capital retained to grow the balance sheet at Schwab's ~7% Tier-1 leverage operating target: retention = k x revenue growth, k = 0.8 base (1.0 and 0.9 in FY2027-28) / 0.6 bull / 1.2 bear (TCE ex-AOCI / revenue ~1.24x, so k = 1.2 is one-for-one capital growth; 0.8 reflects that ~half of revenue is asset-based fees and trading that consume little capital). Working-capital capture 0. Result: FCFE = adjusted net income - retained capital, at the cost of equity; the $6.2B preferred is deducted at par in the bridge rather than its ~$300M/yr dividend charged to the flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine route - UNCHANGED from the 2026-10-02 build (house precedent HBAN, NTRS, NAB.AX, GL): net_debt = 0, preferred deducted in equity_bridge, retention tied to growth. Residual income on tangible book remains rejected as primary because TCE ($25.8B, ~$15/share) is depressed by an -$11.2B AOCI mark and $19.4B of goodwill/intangibles while most earnings are distributed; owner-FCF remains rejected because OCF swings with client cash. UPDATE 2026-11-19 on the Q3-2026 10-Q: (1) anchors refreshed - price, 2026-09-30 balance sheet, 2026-10-30 share count (1,731.0M diluted vs 1,733.3M), buyback pace; (2) FY0 revenue 28,200 -> 28,000; (3) FY2027-28 adjusted pretax margin raised in base (52.5/52.5 -> 53.5/53.0) and bull (54.0/54.5 -> 54.8/55.0); (4) FY2027-28 base retention raised (k 0.8 -> 1.0/0.9). DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: all growth paths, every driver from FY2029 on, the whole bear path, SBC/D&A/tax paths, the 10% cost of equity, terminal growth and caps, and the 25/50/25 weights - see valuation_philosophy.unchanged_assumptions for what would move each. FY0 ANCHOR: FY2026E revenue 28,000, adjusted pretax margin 53.8%, adjusted net income 11,524, less ~390 preferred dividends = ~$6.43 adjusted EPS on 1,731.0M diluted shares (9M actual $4.73; Q3 $1.69 vs ~$1.66 consensus). DATA NOTES: CSV Revenue rows are total net revenues (Q3-2026 7,171 = 10-Q); adjusted figures now also exclude Forge acquisition/integration costs (49 in 9M), which this model follows as genuinely one-off; the Analysis JSON's '14-15% revenue growth' guidance is arithmetically inconsistent with 9M actuals and is not used (see base_revenue_note); D&A 9M-2026 595 (2.9% of revenue) from the 10-Q cash flow statement.

bear.pretax_margin_path_note: UNCHANGED. Implied adjusted pretax margin [43.0, 44.0, 45.0, 45.5, 46.0, 46.0, ...]: a renewed cash-sorting episode (short rates stay high relative to sweep yields) forces Schwab back onto FHLB/brokered funding, NIM compresses and a market drawdown cuts fees and trading; FY2027 revenue falls 6% against a sticky cost base, margin drops toward the FY2024 level (~41.5% adjusted) without reaching the 2023 trough, and recovers only to 46%.
bear.retention_note: UNCHANGED. Retention = 1.2 x revenue growth (one-for-one capital growth) PLUS 1.5% of revenue in FY2027-28 (~$400M/yr) to rebuild leverage capital as supplemental funding re-inflates the balance sheet; in FY2027 that nets to 1.5% because revenue is shrinking (capex 3.8 = 2.3 core + 1.5 rebuild). Terminal cap 12x FCFE for a de-rated rate-sensitive broker-bank.
bear.growth_note: FY2027 -6% (NII -12%, fees -3%, trading -5%), then 2-4.5% recovery on organic NNA that slows to ~4%.

base.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied adjusted pretax margin = EBITDA - SBC - D&A = [53.5, 53.0, 52.0, 51.5, 51.0, 51.0, ...]. CHANGED 2026-11-19, FY2027-28 only (was 52.5, 52.5): FY2026E is now ~53.8% (9M 53.5%, Q3 54.8%), so the old FY2027 figure implied an unexplained 130bp step down from FY0. The path now starts just under the FY2026 level and fades into the UNCHANGED FY2029+ numbers. FY2029 onward (52.0 -> 51.0) is deliberately left alone: one quarter of margin says nothing about the through-cycle spread, and the Q3 detail cuts the other way (lending outgrowing deposits, wholesale borrowings rising, lower floating-rate yields, GAAP expense growth guided up to 10-11%). 51% is ~1pp above FY2025's 50.0% and well above the 2023-24 trough (~38-42%).
base.growth_note: UNCHANGED. FY2027 +8%: core NNA ~5.5-6% plus modest market appreciation on fee assets and residual NIM recovery; fades to 3.5% by FY2036. Q3's record core NNA ($190.4B, +38% YoY; October $66.5B) supports it, but it now compounds from a base 0.7% lower, and sweep-cash softness argues against raising it.
base.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = k x revenue growth. CHANGED 2026-11-19, FY2027-28 only: k raised from 0.8 to 1.0 (FY2027: 8.0% of revenue, ~$2.4B) and 0.9 (FY2028: 6.3%), because 9M-2026 shows the balance sheet absorbing more capital than 0.8x allowed - buybacks fell to $500M in Q3, payout to common ran ~70% of earnings, and adjusted Tier 1 leverage is at the 7.0% top of its objective with loans +25% and margin balances +22% YTD. FY2029+ unchanged at k = 0.8: [5.2, 4.8, 4.4, 4.0, 3.6, 3.6, 3.2, 2.8]% of revenue. FY2027 payout is therefore ~80% of ~$12.4B adjusted net income. Core capex is still modelled equal to D&A (2.3%); 9M-2026 cash capex ran 3.1% of revenue against D&A of 2.9% (plus a $633M debt-financed multi-year software licence), and management now expects FY2026 capex slightly above its 3-5% range - left alone as a one-year item; a second year of capex above D&A would move it.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 10.0%/3.0% on FY2036 FCFE is ~14.7x, below the 16x cap, so Gordon binds. 14.7x FCFE is ~13.5x adjusted earnings - a de-rating from SCHW's ~20x 10-yr average P/E, which is deliberate for a mature, rate-sensitive franchise.

bull.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied adjusted pretax margin [54.8, 55.0, 55.0, ...]. CHANGED 2026-11-19, FY2027-28 only (was 54.0, 54.5): the bull's own premise is that the latest exit rate is the floor, and that rate is now Q3-2026's 54.8% rather than Q2's 53.9%. The 55% plateau is UNCHANGED - Q3 confirms the path, it does not extend it. BDA balances keep returning to the balance sheet, legacy low-yield securities roll into loans (bank lending +35% YoY), and the post-integration cost base delivers operating leverage on record NNA.
bull.retention_note: UNCHANGED: capex_pct - da_pct = 0.6 x revenue growth, on the view that AOCI pull-to-par supplies part of the capital and more growth is capital-light advice fees. Q3 was a step backwards on this (AOCI -11.2B vs -10.6B at June; buybacks $500M), which is why the base case, not the bull, absorbed the retention evidence; a further quarter of sub-$1B buybacks with AOCI flat would move this to 0.8.
bull.growth_note: UNCHANGED. Core NNA holds at 6-7% (Q3-2026 annualised ~5.8% of opening assets, October a record), equity markets compound and managed-investing flows (record $24B in Q3) lift the fee rate.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 25/50/25 (vs the 15/50/35 house default), matching NTRS. Q3 gave evidence in both directions and so moves neither tail: record NNA and a 54.8% margin on one side; on the other, sweep cash fell $7.0B in October, wholesale borrowings are rising again, AOCI widened and buybacks slowed to $500M. Bear stays 25% because rate-path and cash-sorting remain the two high-severity risks with FY2026 earnings near peak NIM; bull stays 25% because it needs record NNA, a held 55% margin and resumed capital release at once, and the stock again failed to rally on a beat.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
